title: Outlet industrial-remnant settlement
scope: Qualitative existence, siting, capability, cultural composition, and story-start rivalry relationship of the initial region's second settlement, built around a reused imperial industrial village nucleus toward the seaward end of the basin's outlet; usable for location, culture, trade, and story development without establishing names, maps, measurements, works detail, resources detail, population, institutions, shore works, events, or any future-conflict or timeline claim.
claims: A second settlement stands in the initial region, built around a reused imperial industrial village nucleus — an instance of WLD-LOCATION-004's reused imperial works node class.
Running water at the settlement site provides a qualitative water-supply and water-power advantage.
Qualitatively workable metal resources occur in the hills near the settlement.
The settlement has grown on the combined strength of its defensible location, its water, and its industrial capability.
The settlement lies on the other side of the basin lake from the initial ridge-spur settlement, toward the seaward end of the outlet, near the outlet's mouth toward the ocean.
The settlement is culturally a primarily imperial-remnant community, in contrast to the initial ridge-spur settlement's blend of original and imperial cultural strands.
Standing tensions and a trade rivalry exist between the two settlements at story start; WLD-EVENT-001 governs that standing pressure.
boundaries: This record is a forward location extension within WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001's initial-region scaffold and an instance of WLD-LOCATION-004's reused imperial works node class; it does not alter the basin lake, regional drainage, climate, coast, outlet, habitat mosaic, migration relationships, the initial ridge-spur settlement, or any accepted journey anchor.

Second, built around, running water, in the hills, near, grown, defensible, other side, toward, seaward end, and mouth are qualitative author-facing relations; no map, distance, direction, bearing, area, elevation, travel time, or other measurement is established.
Second establishes another distinct settlement in the initial region and does not establish a total settlement count, regional exclusivity, or the absence, number, or condition of other communities.

The imperial industrial village is a reused imperial works nucleus, an instance of the class established by WLD-LOCATION-004, which remains the authority for that class; no specific works, layout, building, machine, material, condition, capacity, or imperial-era function is established, and the nucleus's founding date, reuse history, and development sequence remain undefined.

Running water is a qualitative water-supply and water-power advantage only; no watercourse, source, flow, seasonality, reliability, channel, wheel, mill, dam, race, pipe, mechanism, works detail, or all-season guarantee is established.

Metals in the hills are qualitative workable metal resources near the settlement; no ore, deposit, metal type, quantity, quality, mine, working method, smelting practice, fuel, labour, output, trade good, ownership, or exhaustion state is established.

Grown establishes only that the settlement is qualitatively larger or more established than a minor hamlet; its actual size, population, growth history, government, leadership, institutions, law, defences, and economy remain undefined, and no relative size, rank, or comparison with the initial ridge-spur settlement's accepted population range is established.
Defensible location is a qualitative siting advantage; no fortification, wall, gate, garrison, defensive work, defensive performance, or military capability is established.

The position toward the outlet's seaward end, near its mouth toward the ocean, is a qualitative relation consistent with WLD-GEOGRAPHY-001 and WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002, not a mapped location; no shoreline geometry, harbour, anchorage, quay, landing, shore works, coastal practice, or sea use is established.

WLD-GEOGRAPHY-002 continues to establish the outlet mixed-reach feature sequence, and WLD-ECOLOGY-006, WLD-ECOLOGY-009, and WLD-ECOLOGY-010 continue to establish the lake breeding pulse and family-care migrant outlet passage; this record makes no claim about migration, passage, or the mixed reach, places no settlement feature within the outlet throat or reach sequence, and assigns no fishing, harvest, obstruction, disturbance, or other interaction to them.

Primarily imperial-remnant is a qualitative cultural-composition claim; WLD-HISTORY-001 remains the authority for the imperial period, WLD-CULTURE-001 and WLD-CULTURE-002 remain the authorities for the cultural strands themselves, no language, law, belief, practice, institution, dress, craft style, ancestry proportion, internal uniformity, or minority presence is established, and primarily does not mean exclusively.
Cultural identity and contrast are human self-description and interpretation, not natural System behaviour; the System assigns no cultural category, and no System value marks either community.

Standing tensions and trade rivalry are a qualitative story-start relationship whose standing pressure WLD-EVENT-001 governs; this record adds no incident, raid, embargo, blockade, dispute, negotiation, alliance, or other event, and no cause, degree, or expression of the rivalry beyond WLD-EVENT-001.
No future conflict, war, invasion, control assertion, or timeline claim of any kind is established, and no claim that fighting will occur is made; plot intent is staged outside setting canon.
The settlement's name, founding date, precise composition, imperial-era function, current leadership, harbour or shore works, and relations beyond the standing rivalry remain undefined.

The settlement and its relations are author-side setting truth; a character knows the settlement, its people, its capabilities, or the rivalry only through an available source, and familiarity does not reveal composition, intentions, resources, or a System value.
Ordinary finite land, water, metal, matter, energy, labour, time, maintenance, and recovery remain causal where later records establish methods and uses.

No System settlement designation, safe zone, defensive modifier, production bonus, trade mechanic, faction mechanic, reputation value, spawn, reset, automatic repair, free energy, free Mana, or guaranteed recovery is established.
This record changes no CAL0 rule and adopts no WLD-SOUL, WLD-PRENATAL, or other project default.

The cultural contrast between a primarily imperial-remnant community and the ridge-spur settlement's blended strands can expose viewpoint characters to differing customs and self-descriptions without establishing any particular custom, belief, or institution.
The standing tensions and trade rivalry can pressure later choices under WLD-EVENT-001's governance, but no incident, escalation, resolution, or fighting follows automatically.
The author-facing settlement does not become automatic character knowledge; its people, capabilities, and intentions require an available source.

author_approval.evidence: During the 2026-08-17 multiple-choice acceptance session the Author directly specified, rather than selected from displayed options, a second settlement built around an imperial industrial village with running water and metals in the hills, grown on its defensible location, water, and industrial capability, lying on the other side of the basin lake from the ridge-spur settlement near the mouth of the outlet toward the ocean, primarily an imperial-remnant community in contrast to the ridge-spur settlement's blended original-imperial culture, with standing tensions and trade rivalry between the two settlements at story start.
